hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier major #1 reproduced and fixed: a stall in a dispatch of long tasks started a sleep-only back-off because 'slow' was measured at the end of the dispatch. Each laggard now measures its own pickup against slow_at, which only starts once the participants that did start have finished (the pool waits idle with its CPUs freed); finishers decide that with one atomic RMW, so exactly one sees 'only laggards left'.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Deterministic test (test_late_pickup): a worker held off its CPU (SuspendThread / SIGUSR2 handler) 0.15 ms or 1 ms before 2 ms tasks: gen-002 starts a back-off and the next 21 dispatches run sleep-only (p50 = sleeping pool), gen-003 none (p50 0.5 us). Held 3 ms past empty tasks (tid 1 or the last tid), or 2.5 ms past 1 ms tasks: back-off in both. Verifier scenario (16 threads, spin_us=1000, workers-only 2 ms tasks, 4 busy threads, 300 iterations): slow-stall back-offs 0/0/0, short-dispatch mean 0.9 us (verifier on gen-002: 5-8 false back-offs, 13.6-30.8 us). An intermediate version (each finisher stored its finish time, checking pending before its decrement) still counted 7-8 slow stalls at 32 threads: simultaneous finishers all read pending before any decrement.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Caller starvation counts only if the work finished while the caller was off its CPU, measured at the next clock read or when the spin loop sees pending == 0. Before, any gap counted (a caller waiting through long tasks backed off), and a gap that ended inside the poll loop was never measured.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Caller held 0.1-1.5 ms: with 0.3 ms tasks a back-off (gen-002 too), with 3 ms tasks none (gen-002: back-off). Without the exit check the 0.3 ms case was missed in every run (the hold lands in the poll loop).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier major #2 reproduced and fixed: idle spinners' yields handed CPUs to other processes. Workers yield for late threads (a participant has not picked up the newest dispatch, or pending == 0 and the caller has not returned) only in crowded pools (n_threads > 3/4 of hx_num_cpus()); every worker still yields after 50 us without a task; the caller yields only in crowded pools, from its first stall check.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: v_engine, spin_us=50, 10 us regions, interleaved, us per region (base / gen-002 / gen-003): 16 threads + 16 busy 11.6-29.5 / 48-88 / 11.5-12.7; with 20 us caller gaps 33.4-39.2 / 77-166 / 32.5-38.9; 24 + 8 busy 14.9-23.5 / 35.6-43.3 / 13.2-16.7; 28 + 4 busy 56.6-118.9 / 32-42.5 / 31.8-48.8; 32 + 4 busy 108-119 / 37-43 / 34.9-44. test_small_pool_load (16 threads + 20 busy): gen-003 11.3-18.8 us vs sleeping 45-53 us; gen-002 65.6 vs 47.6 (fails).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Conditional yields remain necessary in crowded pools: on this (never quiet) machine nearly every 32-thread dispatch has a displaced participant that only a yield brings back.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: 32 threads, spin_us=1000: without yields for late threads (stall rule only) p50 55-60 us; with them 5-8 us; base 1.0 ms. Delaying the first yield to 5 / 10 us moves p50 to 7.8 / 12.9 us, also at HIGH priority class. test_full_machine (Windows) fails with crowded forced to 0 (p50 54.7 vs sleeping 78.8 us).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier minor #3 (WSL2 16-thread tail) fixed: in pools that are not crowded the stall threshold is max(20 us, (k-1) x wake cost) (2x and at least 200 us for dispatches that woke workers) and the slow-stall / caller-starved threshold max(0.5 ms, 4x re-wake). The wake cost is the caller's own signalling time per woken worker (EMA, weight 1/4): ~2 us on Windows, ~17 us under WSL2.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: WSL2 v_lat interleaved, share of time in > 100 us dispatches (p999): 16 threads base 0.7-1.8% (34-41 us), gen-002 29-32% (280-285 us), gen-003 0-1.6% (27-37 us); 24 threads 16-25% / 44-51% / 5.8-7.0%. test_core_pool_tail fails on gen-002 under WSL2 (16-34%) and passes on gen-003 (0.5-5.4%). test_stall_threshold (seeded wake cost): no stall at 0.4x, stall at 2x, crowded pool at 20 us, slow only after 4x re-wake; it fails with the scaling removed.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Back-off doubling keys on spinning dispatches: a new sleep-only period within 16 spinning dispatches of the last one is twice as long, otherwise 10 ms (was: within 4x the last period's length in time).
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_backoff_period: 10, 20, then (after 40 spinning dispatches) 10 ms. With 2 ms worker tasks at 32 threads the old rule plus the old slow measure kept the pool sleep-only most of the time (short dispatches 54-61 us); now 0 slow stalls, 13.7 us.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Platform minors: hx_env_double keeps an underflowing value (subnormal or zero) on both platforms (glibc sets ERANGE for both, the MS CRT only for zero); POSIX hx_file_replace logs the directory fsync at debug level and a child-process test checks it.
hypotheses_validated.evidence: test_platform against gen-002's platform_common.inc fails 3 checks on Linux (1e-320, -4.9e-324, 1e-400) and 1 on Windows (1e-400). Deleting the hx__sync_parent call fails test_replace_sync under WSL2 (mutant M0483 killed).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Yielding only while some pool thread is late (no crowded rule) stops the oversubscription cascade.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: 16 threads + 16 busy, 10 us regions: 39-51 us per region (base 12); 20-24 threads + 4-8 busy: 31-50 vs 13-17 us. A yield turns a running pool thread into a queued one whenever another thread waits on that CPU, so lateness spreads.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: A per-thread pause after long yields (> 10-50 us) separates harmful from useful yields.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: The long-yield fraction is 8-19% in both regimes (32 threads alone 11%, 16 + 16 busy 19%); penalties that fixed 16 + 16 (13-18 us) broke 32 threads (42-62 us), those that kept 32 threads did not fix 16 + 16.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: Scaling the thresholds with the wake cost also in crowded pools helps WSL2 at no cost.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: WSL2 32 threads: v_lat 340-480 us with it vs 620-770 us without, but test_stranded (32 + 16 busy) spent 23-60% of its time in > 2 ms dispatches with it; without it 14-40% (gen-002 9.5-29.8%), so the host noise dominates. Crowded pools keep 20 us / 0.5 ms (gen-002's Windows-tuned values).

hypotheses_falsified.claim: The quiet-machine target (32-thread dispatch within a small multiple of 16-thread) can be shown on this machine.
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Never quiet (~8.6 CPUs of normal-priority load). Even with the bench at HIGH priority class nearly every 32-thread dispatch needs a yield (p50 5.2-5.4 us; delaying the first yield shifts p50 by the delay); 16 threads 0.75 us: ~7-9x. Base at HIGH priority: p50 0.9 us but p90 1.0 ms, mean 133 us.

open_questions: WSL2 32-thread pools: gen-003 mean 622-768 us vs base 204-240 us and gen-002 771-803 us (interleaved). Every variant tried stays at 0.2-0.9 ms there; native Linux untested. Engine callers should keep n_threads <= physical cores on VMs.

Linux CFS: after sched_yield the CPU goes to the thread with the least run time (another spinner), so a pool pinned to one CPU with a long spin window leaves the caller about a third of its CPU (2.9-3.0x, gen-002 the same). test_pinned judges that ratio on Windows only; sleeping instead of yielding would be the fix there.

Surviving pool.c mutants (40 of 168): equivalent (>= vs > on clock values, initial values overwritten by memset, cap comparisons below the cap, starved = 2, idle_yield > vs >=), tuning constants (4x starve, 2x wake-dispatch threshold, (k-1) vs k in the re-wake cost, EMA weight, crowded caller's first-yield time), the crowded caller's yield-gap starvation check (reachable only when the caller is preempted inside SwitchToThread), the caller's `done` store (removing it gives gen-002-like yields in crowded pools) and the spurious-yield guard in hx__late (perf only).
Test hooks hx__pool_stats / hx__pool_seed_wake are exported from pool.c (not declared in hx_pool.h) and declared by test_pool.c itself; see contract_issues.
